documents.title: Safety Zone; Huron River, Huron, OH
documents.abstract: The Coast Guard is establishing a temporary safety zone for navigable waters of the Huron River within a 150-yard radius of 41[deg]23'34.6" N, 82[deg]33'07.7" W in Huron, OH. The safety zone is needed to protect personnel, vessels, and the marine environment from potential hazards created by an over water fireworks show. Entry of vessels or persons into this zone is prohibited unless specifically authorized by the Captain of the Port, Sector Detroit, or their designated representative.

documents.title: Accuracy of Advertising and Notice of Insured Status
documents.abstract: The NCUA Board (Board) is issuing this final rule to streamline its regulations governing advertising and the notice of insured status. This final rule eliminates provisions concerning the official advertising statement. This action is undertaken to reduce regulatory complexity, and the intended effect is to reduce the administrative burden and costs for federally insured credit unions (FICUs) and provide them with greater flexibility in their advertising activities. The final rule does not amend requirements related to displaying the official sign.

documents.title: Privacy of Consumer Financial Information
documents.abstract: The NCUA Board (Board) is issuing a final rule to make technical corrections to provisions of the NCUA's regulations. The technical amendments improve clarity by removing obsolete references to the privacy of consumer financial information regulation, which the NCUA no longer administers.

documents.title: Nondiscrimination Requirements
documents.abstract: The NCUA Board (Board) is publishing this final rule to remove a redundant and outdated regulation regarding nondiscrimination in lending. The regulation was intended to summarize the Fair Housing Act (FHA) prohibitions on discrimination related to real estate related loans, appraisals, and advertising. The Board's last substantive amendment to the regulation was finalized in 2001. Thus, the regulation does not reflect all case law or regulatory developments under the FHA, a statute that primarily falls under the jurisdiction of the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) and continues to apply to federal credit unions (FCUs) regardless of this regulation. For these reasons, the Board is removing the regulation in its entirety.

documents.title: Registration of Mortgage Loan Originators
documents.abstract: The NCUA Board (Board) is issuing a final rule to make technical corrections to provisions of the NCUA's regulations. The technical amendments in this final rule improve clarity by removing obsolete references to the registration of mortgage loan originators.

documents.title: Restoring Flexibility To Support Head Start Program Access
documents.abstract: In this final rule, the Administration for Children and Families (ACF) removes requirements from the Head Start Program Performance Standards (Performance Standards) to restore local flexibility to Head Start programs and improve access to quality services. Specifically, this final rule removes requirements related to wages and benefits that the Administration believes are not in line with the plain language of the Head Start Act and are costly and overly prescriptive for Head Start programs and staff. ACF estimates these changes will result in over $2 billion in future cost savings for Head Start programs. The rescissions in this final rule impact the costliest parts of the final rule published by the Office of Head Start (OHS) in 2024, Supporting the Head Start Workforce and Consistent Quality Programming.

documents.title: Review of Submarine Cable Landing License Rules and Procedures To Assess Evolving National Security, Law Enforcement, Foreign Policy, and Trade Policy Risks
documents.abstract: On July 8, 2026, the Federal Communications Commission announced the effective date of the Commission's rules. That document inadvertently failed to update the effective date in amendatory instructions 13, 17, and 19. This document corrects the final regulations.

documents.title: Fisheries of the Exclusive Economic Zone off Alaska; Pelagic Trawl Gear Definition
documents.abstract: NMFS proposes regulations to revise the regulatory definition of authorized fishing gear, including the definition of pelagic trawl gear, and the gear limitations for pelagic trawl gear, applicable to vessels in the exclusive economic zone (EEZ) off Alaska. This action is necessary to clearly allow the use of certain common components in codends and bycatch reduction devices, and to remove an outdated limitation on the use of parallel line trawls. This action is expected to provide additional flexibility and promote innovations in pelagic trawl gear design, which may reduce environmental impacts while maintaining efficient fishing operations. This action is intended to promote the goals and objectives of the Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act (Magnuson-Stevens Act), the Fishery Management Plan (FMP) for Groundfish of the Gulf of Alaska Management Area (GOA FMP) and the FMP for Groundfish of the Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands Management Area (BSAI FMP), and other applicable laws.

documents.title: Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards; Modernization of FMVSS No. 108 To Accommodate ADS-Equipped Vehicles
documents.abstract: In response to requests from the Alliance for Automotive Innovation (the Alliance), Society of Automotive Engineers (SAE) International, and Gatik AI Inc. (Gatik), NHTSA is announcing a 15-day extension of the public comment period for the notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM) published on October 26, 2026 proposing to amend Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) No. 108, "Lamps, reflective devices, and associated equipment." The proposed modifications would distinguish how regulations apply to vehicles with and without manually operated driving controls. The comment period for the notice was originally scheduled to end on November 25, 2026. It will now end on December 10, 2026.

documents.title: Air Plan Approval; AK; Fairbanks PM2.5 Boundary Redesignation and Clean Data Determination
documents.abstract: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is proposing to approve a request from Alaska to revise the boundary designation of the existing Fairbanks North Star Borough nonattainment area for the 2006 primary 24-hour fine particulate matter (PM<INF>2.5</INF>) National Ambient Air Quality Standard (NAAQS). The EPA is proposing to split the existing nonattainment area into two distinct nonattainment areas, an area covering Fairbanks and the Goldstream Valley, and an area covering North Pole. The proposed new areas cover the same geographic area as the existing area. The EPA is also proposing to issue a clean data determination (CDD), for the proposed Fairbanks and Goldstream Valley area ("proposed Fairbanks nonattainment area") based on a determination that the area is attaining the 2006 PM<INF>2.5</INF> NAAQS. If the EPA finalizes this CDD, certain Clean Air Act (CAA) requirements that apply to the proposed Fairbanks nonattainment area will be suspended for so long as the area continues to meet the 2006 24-hour PM<INF>2.5</INF> NAAQS. The EPA is taking this action pursuant to Clean Air Act sections 107, 110, 172, and 189.

documents.title: Special Local Regulation: Marine Events Within the Captain of the Port Miami, Seminole Hard Rock Winterfest Holiday Boat Parade
documents.abstract: The Coast Guard will enforce a special local regulation to provide for the safety of life on navigable waterways during the Seminole Hard Rock Winterfest Holiday Boat Parade. Our regulation for marine events within the Captain of the Port Miami identifies the regulated area for this event in Fort Lauderdale, FL. All non- participant persons and vessels are prohibited from entering, transiting, anchoring, or remaining within the regulated area during the enforcement period unless authorized by the Captain of the Port Miami or a designated representative. The operator of any vessel in the regulated area must comply with directions from the Coast Guard or designated representative.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; Dassault Aviation Airplanes
documents.abstract: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Dassault Aviation Model FALCON 6X airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by a determination that new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations are necessary. This proposed AD would require revising the existing maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, to incorporate new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Castle Mountains National Monument and Craters of the Moon National Monument; Hunting
documents.abstract: The National Park Service (NPS) proposes to promulgate special regulations to allow hunting in Castle Mountains National Monument and Craters of the Moon National Monument. The regulations would recognize the authority of the States to manage wildlife while also allowing for appropriate management of hunting by the NPS to protect public health and safety, objects of historic and scientific interest that the Monuments were established to protect, and endangered or threatened species. Allowing hunting in these National Monuments is directed by Executive Order 14429, "Reinvigorating America's Hunting Heritage," and advances the policy of the Trump Administration to reinvigorate, protect, and expand America's hunting heritage to benefit our people and our land.

documents.title: Surety Bond Guarantee Program: Streamlining and Modernizing
documents.abstract: This final rule makes several changes to the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) Surety Bond Guarantee (SBG) program regulations. The rule reduces the burden on participating surety companies for submission and retention of documents. The rule also corrects conflicting provisions, as well as revising the obsolete Preferred Surety admissions requirements and the Quarterly Contract Completion Report.

documents.title: Dole State and Tribal Outreach Grant Program
documents.abstract: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is proposing regulations to implement the Dole State and Tribal Outreach Grant Program (DSTOGP), as authorized under the Senator Elizabeth Dole 21st Century Veterans Healthcare and Benefits Improvement Act. This program aids veterans and their families by awarding funding to eligible organizations to carry out programs to improve covered outreach and assistance to ensure that veterans and their families are fully informed about, and assisted in applying for, any veterans and veterans-related benefits and programs (including veterans programs of a State or Indian Tribe) for which they may be eligible.

documents.title: Air Plan Partial Approval and Partial Conditional Approval; South Carolina; Minor Source Permit Program Revisions and Control of Oxides of Nitrogen and Source Testing Requirements
documents.abstract: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA or Agency) is approving changes to South Carolina's State Implementation Plan (SIP) which revise the State's source testing requirements and its regulations prescribing minor source permit program requirements, including minor new source review (NSR) requirements, and partially approving and partially conditionally approving regulations prescribing control requirements for certain stationary sources of nitrogen oxides (NO<INF>X</INF>) in SIP revisions submitted by the State of South Carolina, through the South Carolina Department of Environmental Services (SC DES), on October 1, 2007; July 18, 2011; June 17, 2013; August 8, 2014; January 20, 2016; July 27, 2016; September 5, 2017; April 24, 2020; February 4, 2022; and July 23, 2025. This action is being finalized pursuant to the Clean Air Act (CAA or Act).

documents.title: Safety Zone; FRL Inaugural Invitational eFoil Exhibition Race, Miami Marine Stadium Basin, Miami, FL
documents.abstract: The Coast Guard is establishing a temporary safety zone for certain navigable waters of the Miami Marine Stadium Basin in connection with the FRL Inaugural Invitational eFoil Exhibition Race. This safety zone is necessary to protect personnel, vessels, and the marine environment from potential hazards associated with the eFoil races. This rule prohibits entry of vessels or persons into this safety zone unless authorized by the Captain of the Port Sector Miami or its designated representative.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH (AHD) Helicopters
documents.abstract: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH (AHD) Model MBB-BK 117 C-1 and MBB-BK 117 C-2 helicopters with a certain air conditioning system installed in accordance with FAA Supplemental Type Certificate (STC) No. SR00601DE. This proposed AD was prompted by reports of corrosion on the condenser inlet duct, which caused the internal support wire helix to impinge the tail rotor (TR) drive shaft. This proposed AD would require repetitively inspecting the TR drive shaft; repetitively inspecting the exterior of the Air Comm Corporation (ACC) condenser duct assembly (duct assembly); repetitively inspecting (using a borescope) the interior of the ACC duct assembly; and depending on the results of these inspections, replacing certain parts. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters
documents.abstract: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2025-24-01, which applies to all Airbus Helicopters Model EC 155 B and EC 155 B1 helicopters. AD 2025-24-01 requires replacement of the jettisonable windows and seals on the sliding doors and fixed panels on the left-hand (LH) and right-hand (RH) sides and the installation of new labels. Since the FAA issued AD 2025-24-01, the manufacturer determined the applicable service information was missing procedures for the tinted windows. This proposed AD would require the same actions as AD 2025-24-01 and would additionally require new actions to include helicopters with the modification of tinted windows. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes
documents.abstract: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain The Boeing Company Model 787-8 airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by a report that certain wing skin outer mold line (OML) penetrating fasteners installed using threaded nuts without cap seals do not provide reliable protection against potential ignition sources when subjected to direct attachment lightning currents. This proposed AD would require inspecting between certain ribs on the left and right wing for wing skin penetrating fasteners with a threaded nut adjacent to the electromagnetic effects (EME) sleeve; inspecting the left and right wing fuel tanks, surge tanks, and dry bays for threaded nuts installed on fasteners that penetrate the upper and lower wing skins; accomplishing the inspection specified in a certain airworthiness limitation (AWL); and applicable on-condition actions. This proposed AD would also require accomplishing concurrent requirements and revising the maintenance program to incorporate the airworthiness limitation task. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Publication of Iran-Related Web General Licenses EE and FF
documents.abstract: The Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) is publishing two Iran-related general licenses (GLs): GLs EE and FF, which were made available on OFAC's website at the time of issuance.

documents.title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 55F and 115D
documents.abstract: The Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) is publishing two general licenses (GLs) issued pursuant to the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations: GLs 55F and 115D, each of which was previously made available on OFAC's website.

documents.title: Publication of a Cuba Sanctions Regulations Web General License
documents.abstract: The Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) is publishing a general license (GL) issued in the Cuba Sanctions program: GL 1. This GL was previously made available on OFAC's website.

documents.title: Amendment of Class C Airspace; Laughlin Air Force Base, Del Rio, TX
documents.abstract: This action makes administrative amendments to the Laughlin AFB, TX, Class C airspace legal description. Specifically, the action updates the geographic coordinates of the airport reference point (ARP) to match the FAA's National Airspace System Resources (NASR) database information. Additionally, this action corrects the header format to conform with current FAA policy. Lastly, this action updates the outdated term "Airport/Facility Directory" to "Chart Supplement." This action does not change the lateral boundaries, altitudes, or operating requirements of the Class C airspace area.

documents.title: Publication of Iran-Related Web General License W
documents.abstract: The Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) is publishing an Iran-related general license (GL): GL W. This GL was previously made available on OFAC's website.

documents.title: Update to Statutory Citations and Internet Address in Bid Protest Regulations
documents.abstract: The Government Accountability Office (GAO) is issuing a final rule to amend its Bid Protest Regulations, promulgated in accordance with the Competition in Contracting Act of 1984 (CICA), to make an administrative change by updating citations to the United States Code to reflect amendment and recodification of underlying statutory provisions. The revisions only reflect changes that update an internet address and that update statutory citations to reflect statutory changes, so GAO has determined that the rule is uncontroversial and therefore it is appropriate to issue a final rule.

documents.title: Safety Zone; Massachusetts Bay, Boston, MA
documents.abstract: The Coast Guard is establishing temporary moving safety zones for certain portions of the navigable water of Massachusetts Bay, 22 miles northeast of Boston, MA. The safety zones are needed to protect personnel, vessels, and the maritime public from potential hazards created by subsea demolition operations. Entry of vessels or persons into this zone is prohibited unless specifically authorized by the Captain of the Port, Sector Boston, or their designated representative.

documents.title: Oil and Gas and Sulfur Operations in the Outer Continental Shelf-Revisions to the Requirements for Exploratory Drilling on the Arctic Outer Continental Shelf; Reopening of Comment Period
documents.abstract: The Department of the Interior (DOI or Department), acting through MMA, is reopening the comment period for Proposed Rule: Oil and Gas and Sulfur Operations in the Outer Continental Shelf--Revisions to the Requirements for Exploratory Drilling on the Arctic Outer Continental Shelf, which was published in the Federal Register on August 6, 2026.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes
documents.abstract: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all The Boeing Company Model 747-400 and 747-400F series airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by a report of an overheated alternating current motor pump (ACMP) that caused a fire in the main landing gear (MLG) wheel well. This proposed AD would require a maintenance records check or inspection for any installed ACMP with a certain part number and applicable on-condition actions. This proposed AD would also prohibit the installation of affected parts. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Air Plan Approval; Oregon Department of Environmental Quality; Emission Standards and Controls for Sources Emitting Gasoline Vapors
documents.abstract: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) proposes to approve a revision to the Oregon State Implementation Plan (SIP) submitted by the Oregon Department of Environmental Quality (ODEQ) on December 17, 2025, for the Portland and Salem/Keizer, Oregon 1979 1-hour ozone maintenance areas. The proposed revision updates ODEQ's requirements in the SIP for Stages I and II vapor recovery systems at gasoline dispensing facilities including: decommissioning existing Stage II systems incompatible with onboard refueling vapor recovery systems; allowing removal from service of Stage II vapor recovery equipment compatible with onboard refueling vapor recovery; and removing the requirement for Stage II vapor recovery at new installations. The proposed revisions also include more widespread adoption of Stage I Enhanced Vapor Recovery, Stage I vapor balance, and enhanced conventional nozzles, among other changes. The EPA is proposing to find that ODEQ's demonstration to remove Stage II requirements is consistent with the Clean Air Act and the EPA's guidance.

documents.title: Common Crop Insurance Regulations; Apple Crop Insurance Provisions; Withdrawal
documents.abstract: This action informs the public that the Federal Crop Insurance Corporation (FCIC) is withdrawing a notice of proposed rulemaking with request for comments published in the Federal Register on December 16, 2021, titled Common Crop Insurance Regulations, Apple Crop Insurance Provisions. FCIC has determined that rulemaking is not necessary or appropriate at this time based on comments received in response to the proposed changes. If FCIC decides to pursue future regulatory action on this topic, it will issue a new proposed rule.

documents.title: Air Plan Approval; Utah; Update to Materials Incorporated by Reference
documents.abstract: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is updating the materials that are incorporated by reference (IBR) into the Utah State Implementation Plan (SIP). The regulations affected by this update have been previously submitted by Utah and approved by the EPA. In this final rule, the EPA is also notifying the public of corrections and clarifying changes in the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) tables that identify material IBR into the Utah SIP. This update affects the materials that are available for public inspection at the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) and the EPA Regional Office.

documents.title: Ethephon; Pesticide Tolerances
documents.abstract: This regulation establishes tolerances for residues of ethephon in or on fig. Under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FFDCA), Interregional Research Project Number 4 (IR-4) submitted a petition to EPA requesting that EPA establish a maximum permissible level for residues of this pesticide in or on the identified commodity.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; Pratt & Whitney Canada Corp. Engines
documents.abstract: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Pratt & Whitney Canada Corp. (P&WC) Model PW814GA and PW815GA engines. This proposed AD was prompted by the manufacturer revising the airworthiness limitations section (ALS) of the existing airworthiness limitations manual (ALM) to introduce new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations and associated thresholds and intervals for life-limited parts. This proposed AD would require updating the ALS of the existing ALM or instructions for continued airworthiness (ICA) and the existing approved maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, to incorporate new or more restrictive instructions and associated thresholds and intervals for life-limited parts. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; General Electric Company Engines
documents.abstract: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain General Electric Company (GE) Model GE Passport 20-17BB1A, GE Passport 20-18BB1A, GE Passport 20-19BB1A, and GE Passport 20-19BB1B engines. This proposed AD was prompted by an engine in-flight shutdown (IFSD) due to an engine fire caused by fuel leakage within the engine core compartment. This proposed AD would require replacement of a certain start bleed valve (SBV) fuel tube with a redesigned SBV fuel tube. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Isocycloseram; Pesticide Tolerance for Emergency Exemption
documents.abstract: This regulation establishes a time-limited tolerance for residues of isocycloseram, including its metabolites and degradates, in or on sunflowers. This action is in response to EPA's authorization of a specific exemption under the Federal Insecticide, Fungicide, and Rodenticide Act (FIFRA) authorizing use of the pesticide on sunflowers. This regulation establishes a maximum permissible level for residues of isocycloseram in or on sunflower, seed at 0.4 parts per million. The time-limited tolerance expires on December 31, 2029.

documents.title: Revocation of the Color Additive Listing for Use of Orange B on Casings or Surfaces of Frankfurters and Sausages; Confirmation of Effective Date
documents.abstract: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or we) is confirming the effective date of September 8, 2026, for the final order that appeared in the Federal Register of July 23, 2026, and that repealed the color additive regulation that allows for the use of Orange B for coloring the casings or surfaces of frankfurters and sausages.

documents.title: Amendment of Class C Airspace; President Donald J. Trump International Airport, FL
documents.abstract: This action proposes to amend Class C airspace at the President Donald J. Trump International Airport (DJT), West Palm Beach, FL. The FAA is proposing this action to enhance the efficient management of air traffic operations and reduce the potential for midair collision in the West Palm Beach, FL, terminal area.

documents.title: Horse Protection
documents.abstract: On May 8, 2024, the Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS) of the United States Department of Agriculture published in the Federal Register a final rule that amended the regulations promulgated under the Horse Protection Act (the May 2024 Horse Protection final rule). APHIS is proposing to remove the provisions of the May 2024 Horse Protection final rule that have been vacated by court order and proposing to withdraw the remaining non-vacated provisions of the May 2024 Horse Protection final rule to ensure that the regulations afford due process and better align with the Act. APHIS is also proposing to amend the regulations by revising, among other things, the certification requirements for training and licensing of designated qualified persons (DQPs); enhancing DQP inspection procedures and the process for appealing APHIS inspections before any possible disqualification by management; and clarifying that if a horse is determined to be sore, it is disqualified from participating in the class in which the inspection took place and not the entire event.

documents.title: AP1000 Design Certification Renewal
Schedules of Controlled Substances: Placement of Oveporexton in Schedule IV
documents.abstract: On August 5, 2026, the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved a new drug application for Orzeyful (oveporexton) for the treatment of narcolepsy type 1 in adults. The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) provided the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) with a scheduling recommendation to place oveporexton, chemically known as N-[(2S,3R)-2-[[3-(3,5- difluorophenyl)-2-fluorophenyl]methyl]-4,4-difluoro-1-(2-hydroxy-2- methylpropanoyl)pyrrolidin-3-yl]ethanesulfonamide, in schedule IV of the Controlled Substances Act (CSA). In accordance with the CSA, as amended by the Improving Regulatory Transparency for New Medical Therapies Act, DEA is hereby issuing an interim final rule placing oveporexton, including its salts, isomers and salts of isomers whenever the existence of such salts, isomers, and salts of isomers is possible, in schedule IV of the CSA.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; Dassault Aviation Airplanes
documents.abstract: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Dassault Aviation Model MYSTERE-FALCON 50, FALCON 2000, and FALCON 2000EX airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by a reported quality escape and a determination that high-temperature oxidation of main landing gear (MLG) upper and lower torque links may have occurred during manufacturing. This proposed AD would require replacing any affected MLG with a serviceable MLG. This proposed AD would also limit the installation of affected parts under certain conditions. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Standard Instrument Approach Procedures, and Takeoff Minimums and Obstacle Departure Procedures; Miscellaneous Amendments
documents.abstract: This rule amends, suspends, or removes Standard Instrument Approach Procedures (SIAPs) and associated Takeoff Minimums and Obstacle Departure Procedures for operations at certain airports. These regulatory actions are needed because of the adoption of new or revised criteria, or because of changes occurring in the National Airspace System, such as the commissioning of new navigational facilities, adding new obstacles, or changing air traffic requirements. These changes are designed to provide for the safe and efficient use of the navigable airspace and to promote safe flight operations under instrument flight rules at the affected airports.

documents.title: Standard Instrument Approach Procedures, and Takeoff Minimums and Obstacle Departure Procedures; Miscellaneous Amendments
documents.abstract: This rule establishes, amends, suspends, or removes Standard Instrument Approach Procedures (SIAPS) and associated Takeoff Minimums and Obstacle Departure procedures (ODPs) for operations at certain airports. These regulatory actions are needed because of the adoption of new or revised criteria, or because of changes occurring in the National Airspace System, such as the commissioning of new navigational facilities, adding new obstacles, or changing air traffic requirements. These changes are designed to provide safe and efficient use of the navigable airspace and to promote safe flight operations under instrument flight rules at the affected airports.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; Diamond Aircraft Industries GmbH Airplanes
documents.abstract: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Diamond Aircraft Industries GmbH (DAI) Model DA 50 C airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by reports of flap actuator failures. This proposed AD would require inspecting for displacement of the black slide grommet and inspecting the rod end bearing for a tight fit of the flap actuator. This proposed AD would also require modification of the flap actuator followed by repetitive inspections for a broken actuator torque seal on the jam nuts at the attachment of the rod end bearing of the flap actuator with applicable corrective action. This proposed AD would also prohibit the installation of unmodified flap actuators on any airplane. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Authorization To Manufacture and Distribute Postage Evidencing Systems
documents.abstract: The Postal Service is amending its Postage Evidencing Systems regulations to align with existing practices and operational realities to better address circumstances where advances by a resetting company on any given day exceed the daily average funds advanced amount maintained on deposit with the Postal Service. The regulations currently allow resetting companies to advance postage to customers by a process where the resetting company maintains a daily average advance balance with the Postal Service. The current regulation contemplates that the amount on deposit will always cover amounts advanced and does not permit a resetting company to advance funds to customers in excess of the amount maintained on deposit. Operational realities will create circumstances where it is necessary to advance funds in excess of the amount on deposit and the average daily balance rule represents a practical and fair method to address circumstances where excess advances occur.

documents.title: Federal Reserve Bank Capital Stock
documents.abstract: The Board of Governors (Board) is publishing a final rule that applies an inflation adjustment to the threshold for total consolidated assets in Regulation I. Federal Reserve Bank (Reserve Bank) stockholders that have total consolidated assets above the threshold receive a different dividend rate on their Reserve Bank stock than stockholders with total consolidated assets at or below the threshold. The Federal Reserve Act requires that the Board annually adjust the total consolidated asset threshold to reflect the change in the Gross Domestic Product Price Index, published by the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). Based on the change in the Gross Domestic Product Price Index as of September 30, 2026, the total consolidated asset threshold will be $13,712,000,000 through December 31, 2027.

documents.title: Mining of Pillars
documents.abstract: MSHA is eliminating outdated requirements for the final mining of pillars from MSHA's regulations. These requirements are being removed because the practice of final mining of pillars with one mine opening is no longer used in the mining industry due to safety concerns.

documents.title: Electrical Equipment for Coal Seams Above the Water Table
documents.abstract: MSHA is removing requirements for the use of permissible electric face equipment in coal seams above the water table. These requirements are being removed from MSHA's regulations because all coal mines are now considered gassy, regardless of location relative to the water table.

documents.title: Improving and Eliminating Regulations; Installation of Foam Generator Systems in Underground Coal Mines
documents.abstract: MSHA is removing outdated requirements regarding the installation of foam generator systems located in underground coal mines. These requirements are being removed from MSHA's regulations because they are no longer applicable.

documents.title: Improving and Eliminating Regulations; Limit on Exposure to Diesel Particulate Matter in Underground Metal and Nonmetal Mines
documents.abstract: MSHA is eliminating outdated requirements for diesel particulate matter (DPM) personal exposure limits for underground metal and nonmetal (MNM) mines. These requirements are being removed from MSHA's regulations because they contain outdated effective dates and exposure limits that are no longer applicable.

documents.title: Improving and Eliminating Regulations; Permissible Lamps in Underground Coal Mines
documents.abstract: MSHA is removing duplicative requirements for electric cap lamps and other electric lamps in underground coal mines. This provision is being removed from MSHA's regulations because it is a duplicative provision and its removal will not reduce the protections afforded to miners.

documents.title: Respirable Crystalline Silica and Respiratory Protection
documents.abstract: This proposed rule clarifies and modifies provisions of the respirable crystalline silica and respiratory protection standards that were established in MSHA's 2024 final rule titled "Lowering Miners' Exposure to Respirable Crystalline Silica and Improving Respiratory Protection." The changes provide clarity and make improvements to the requirements for methods of compliance, exposure monitoring, respiratory protection, medical surveillance, and recordkeeping while maintaining strong protection of miners. The proposal also includes related conforming amendments.

documents.title: Special Local Regulation; Southern California Annual Marine Events for the San Diego Captain of the Port Zone, San Diego Fleet Week Veterans Day Boat Parade, San Diego Bay, San Diego, CA
documents.abstract: The Coast Guard will enforce a special local regulation for the San Diego Fleet Week Veterans Day Boat Parade on November 11, 2026, to provide for the safety of life on navigable waterways during this event. Our regulation for marine events within the Southwest Coast Guard District identifies the regulated area for this event in San Diego, CA. During the enforcement periods, the operator of any vessel in the regulated area must comply with directions from the Patrol Commander or any Official Patrol displaying a Coast Guard ensign.

documents.title: Television Broadcasting Services, St. George, Utah
documents.abstract: This document amends the Table of TV Allotments (Table) of the Federal Communications Commission's (Commission) rules by substituting VHF channel 9 for UHF channel 21 at St. George, Utah in response to a petition for rulemaking filed by KUTV Licensee, LLC (Licensee), licensee of full power television station KMYU(TV) (KMYU or Station), St. George, Utah. The Media Bureau (Bureau) previously granted a petition for rulemaking submitted by the Licensee to substitute UHF channel 21 for VHF channel 9 at St. George, Utah in the Table. The Licensee subsequently filed an application for a construction permit for its new channel, which remains pending due to certain unresolved engineering matters. The Licensee now states that upon further consideration and restraints, it wishes to abandon its plans to modify its license for KMYU to operate on channel 21. The Licensee filed the instant petition to amend the Table to substitute VHF channel 9 for UHF channel 21 and allow KMYU to continue to operate on channel 9 at its licensed parameters. The staff engineering analysis finds that the proposal is in compliance with the Commission's principal community coverage and technical requirements, including the interference protection requirements. In support of its channel substitution request, the Licensee filed comments reaffirming its interest and stating that it commits to promptly take any and all steps that may be necessary to effectuate the channel substitution proposed in the petition. An individual commenter, Steven Quinn Singleton (Singleton), also filed comments, but did not explicitly object to the proposed channel change. For the reasons discussed in the Report and Order referenced below, the Bureau denied Singleton's comments.

documents.title: National Television Multiple Ownership Rule
documents.abstract: In this document, the Federal Communications Commission (Commission) repeals the national television multiple ownership rule (national cap), which prohibits a commercial television licensee from having a cognizable interest in television stations that have an aggregate national audience reach above 39%. The Commission finds, given seismic changes in the modern media marketplace, that the rule's repeal will help empower local broadcast television stations to operate in the public interest and to better serve the needs and interests of their local communities. The Commission will review on a case-by-case basis proposed transactions that would have been prohibited under the national cap to determine whether a proposed transaction would serve the Commission's media ownership goals of localism, competition, and viewpoint diversity.

documents.title: Rangeland Management
documents.abstract: The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA or Department) proposes to amend the regulations governing grazing and livestock use on the National Forest System to modernize grazing administration, improve clarity, codify existing policy, and expand opportunities for stewardship and access. The proposed amendments would update permit issuance, eligibility, and qualification provisions; establish a framework for adaptive response to drought, wildfire, and similar disturbance events; and expand authorities for stewardship-oriented livestock use, including adding the ability to implement stewardship projects (such as outcome-based grazing or targeted grazing) under a temporary grazing permit or livestock use permit. The proposed rule would revise grazing fee provisions to ensure consistent fee-setting across the national forests in the 16 contiguous Western States and the national grasslands, and establish a surcharge for authorized leasing of livestock by permittees. It would consolidate and renumber existing sections in subpart A for clarity and make conforming, technical, and administrative updates throughout part 222. The Department invites public comment on all aspects of the proposed rule.

documents.title: Federal Scholarship Tax Credit; Hearing
documents.abstract: This document announces that the public hearing scheduled for December 15, 2026, at 10 a.m. ET, for the notice of proposed rulemaking and notice of public hearing (REG-117199-25) published in the Federal Register on October 2, 2026, has been changed to a telephonic-only hearing. These proposed regulations would provide guidance regarding the non-refundable Federal tax credit for qualified contributions to scholarship granting organizations to fund qualified elementary and secondary school education scholarships.

documents.title: Safety Zone; Sector Mobile Captain of the Port Zone, Mobile, AL
documents.abstract: The Coast Guard is establishing two temporary fixed safety zones to support the arrival and dismantling of the EX ENTERPRISE, formerly the USS ENTERPRISE (CVN-65), in the Sector Mobile Captain of the Port Zone. This rulemaking would prohibit persons and vessels from entering these zones unless authorized by the Captain of the Port, Sector Mobile.

documents.title: Approval and Promulgation of Air Quality Implementation Plans; Michigan; Withdrawal of the Federal Implementation Plan for the Detroit Sulfur Dioxide Area
documents.abstract: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is proposing to withdraw the Federal Implementation Plan (FIP), promulgated on October 12, 2022 (the "2022 FIP"), for attaining the 2010 1-hour primary sulfur dioxide (SO<INF>2</INF>) National Ambient Air Quality Standard (NAAQS) in the Detroit area. On May 19, 2025, the EPA approved a revision to Michigan's State Implementation Plan (SIP) for attaining the 2010 1-hour primary SO<INF>2</INF> NAAQS in the Detroit area, rendering the 2022 FIP duplicative. The EPA is proposing this action pursuant to Clean Air Act (CAA) section 110.

documents.title: Coral, Coral Reefs, and Live/Hardbottom Habitats of the South Atlantic and the Shrimp Fishery of the South Atlantic Region; Amendments 11/12
documents.abstract: NMFS issues this proposed rule to implement Amendment 11 to the Fishery Management Plan for Coral, Coral Reefs, and Live/Hardbottom Habitats of the South Atlantic (Coral FMP) and to implement Amendment 12 to the Fishery Management Plan for the Shrimp Fishery of the South Atlantic Region (Shrimp FMP) (jointly Amendments 11/12), as prepared and submitted by the South Atlantic Fishery Management Council (Council). If implemented, this proposed rule would establish a shrimp fishery access area (SFAA) along the eastern boundary of the northern extension of the Oculina Bank Habitat Area of Particular Concern (OHAPC) where trawling for rock shrimp is currently prohibited. The purpose of this proposed rule is to reinstate access to historic rock shrimp fishing grounds, achieve optimum yield (OY) in the rock shrimp fishery, while minimizing impacts to deep-water corals in the OHAPC.

documents.title: Amendment of Jet Route J-21 in the Vicinity of Laredo, TX
documents.abstract: This action proposes to amend Jet Route J-21 to eliminate an unnecessary 1.47-degree turn in the airway in the vicinity of Laredo, TX. The FAA proposes this action to improve efficiency by straightening the ground track of J-21, eliminating a 1.47-degree turn.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; Bell Textron Canada Limited Helicopters
documents.abstract: The FAA is superseding Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2022-20- 11, which applied to certain Bell Textron Canada Limited Model 429 helicopters. AD 2022-20-11 required visually inspecting the external surface of the tail rotor (TR) gearbox support assembly, borescope inspecting or visually inspecting the inside of the tail boom, and performing a tactile inspection. Depending on the results of the inspections, AD 2022-20-11 required removing certain rivets from service or repairing gaps in accordance with an approved method. Since the FAA issued AD 2022-20-11, the manufacturer determined the repetitive inspection interval needs to be reduced. This AD requires the same actions as AD 2022-20-11 and reduces the inspection interval. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Hematology and Pathology Devices; Reclassification of Immunohistochemistry Test Systems for Use With a Corresponding Approved Oncology Therapeutic Product
documents.abstract: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is proposing to reclassify immunohistochemistry (IHC) test systems indicated for use with a corresponding approved oncology therapeutic product (product codes MVC, NKF, QQT, NQF, PLS, PKW, QUL, QNH, QZJ, SBL, SER, and SHF), which are postamendments class III devices, from class III (premarket approval) into class II (special controls), subject to premarket notification. FDA is proposing minor revisions to an existing classification regulation and also proposing a new device classification regulation, along with the special controls that FDA believes are necessary to provide a reasonable assurance of safety and effectiveness for these devices.

documents.title: Housing and Community Development Act of 1980: Verification of Eligible Status
documents.abstract: This final rule revises HUD's Section 214 regulations to require the verification of U.S. citizenship or the eligible immigration status of all applicants and recipients of assistance under a covered program regardless of age. The rule will also make prorated assistance a temporary condition pending verification of eligible status of all family members, where permitted by statute, as opposed to under HUD's current regulations where prorated assistance could continue indefinitely. These amendments bring HUD's regulations into greater alignment with the wording and purpose of Section 214 and align with the current Administration's priorities and regulatory reform efforts.

documents.title: Fisheries of the Exclusive Economic Zone Off Alaska; Reallocation of Pacific Cod in the Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands Management Area
documents.abstract: NMFS is reallocating the projected unused amounts of Pacific cod from catcher vessels using trawl gear to Amendment 80 (A80) trawl catcher/ processors in the Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands management area (BSAI). This action is necessary to allow the 2026 total allowable catch (TAC) of Pacific cod in the BSAI to be harvested.

documents.title: Imposition of Special Measure Prohibiting the Transmittal of Funds Involving MEXC Global
documents.abstract: FinCEN is issuing notice of an order, pursuant to section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act (Pub. L. 116- 283), as amended by section 6106(b) of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2022 (Pub. L. 117-81), finding that MEXC Global--including any of its subsidiaries, branches, and offices, as well as any successor entities, operating in any jurisdiction outside of the United States--is a financial institution operating outside of the United States of primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance and prohibiting certain transmittals of funds involving MEXC Global.

documents.title: Inspection Programs for Single-Engine Turbine-Powered Airplanes and Unmanned Aircraft; and Miscellaneous Maintenance-Related Updates
documents.abstract: The final rule updates the maintenance inspection requirements for single-engine turbine-powered airplanes and unmanned aircraft. Aircraft owners and operators now have more inspection program options to choose from and more relaxed mechanical reliability reporting requirements. It also clarifies various maintenance-related regulations. This final rule relieves aircraft owners, operators, maintenance providers, and FAA of certain workload burdens by facilitating a more efficient workload for these individuals without compromising aviation safety.

documents.title: Special Conditions: Gulfstream Aerospace Corporation, Model GVII-G400 Airplane; Flight Envelope Protection: Takeoff Stall Protection
documents.abstract: These special conditions are issued for the Gulfstream Aerospace Corporation (Gulfstream) Model GVII-G400 airplane. This airplane will have a novel or unusual design feature when compared to the state of technology envisioned in the airworthiness standards for transport category airplanes. This design feature is an envelope protection function to protect the airplane from over- and rapid- rotation on takeoff. The applicable airworthiness regulations do not contain adequate or appropriate safety standards for this design feature. These special conditions contain the additional safety standards that the Administrator considers necessary to establish a level of safety equivalent to that established by the existing airworthiness standards.

documents.title: Modification to Work Requirements for Able-Bodied Adults
documents.abstract: The proposed rule would codify USDA's regulatory implementation of provisions of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act of 2025 (OBBB) changing the three-month time limit for certain participants subject to work requirements in the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP). These changes include modifying the list of exceptions from the time limit for certain populations; updating requirements for areas to qualify for waivers of the time limit; and adding the temporary good faith exemptions in Alaska and Hawaii. Additionally, this rule proposes to strengthen requirements for requesting waivers of the time limit and revise the SNAP definition of a homeless individual.

documents.title: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program: Reforming Categorical Eligibility
documents.abstract: Under section 5(a) of the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008, households in which each member receives benefits under a State program funded by Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) are categorically eligible for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP). Current SNAP regulations consider TANF benefits to include both cash assistance and non-cash or in-kind benefits or services from TANF-funded programs. This proposal would limit categorical eligibility to only households that receive TANF assistance, as defined at 45 CFR 260.31. These revisions would ensure that SNAP benefits are targeted to needy households that have qualified for TANF assistance while still aligning categorical eligibility's statutory purpose of simplifying program administration. A 100-word summary of this rule has been posted to www.regulations.gov and can be found here.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; Leonardo S.p.a. Helicopters
documents.abstract: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2024-05-07, which applies to all Leonardo S.p.a. Model AW189 helicopters. AD 2024-05-07 requires revising the airworthiness limitations section (ALS) of the existing helicopter maintenance manual or instructions for continued airworthiness (ICA) and the existing approved maintenance or inspection program, as applicable. Since the FAA issued AD 2024-05-07, it was determined that new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations are necessary. This proposed AD would require revising the ALS of the existing maintenance manual or ICA and the existing approved maintenance or inspection program, as applicable. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Canada Limited Partnership (Type Certificate Previously Held by C Series Aircraft Limited Partnership (CSALP); Bombardier, Inc.) Airplanes
documents.abstract: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2021-13-20, which applies to certain Airbus Canada Limited Partnership Model BD-500-1A10 and BD-500-1A11 airplanes. AD 2021-13-20 requires inspecting the waste box, waste access doubler, and waste service door for corrosion, and doing applicable on-condition actions. Since the FAA issued AD 2021-13-20, the FAA has determined that a full secondary fuel vapor barrier must be applied. This proposed AD would retain all requirements of AD 2021-13-20 and would also require, for certain airplanes, an additional inspection of the waste box, waste access doubler, and waste service door for corrosion, and applicable on- condition actions. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus SAS Airplanes; Correction
documents.abstract: The FAA is correcting an airworthiness directive (AD) that was published in the Federal Register. That AD applies to all Airbus SAS Model A330-243, A330-243F, A330-341, A330-342, A330-343, A330-841, and A330-941 airplanes; and Model A340-211, A340-212, A340-213, A340-311, A340-312, A340-313, A340-541, and A340-642 airplanes. As published, a paragraph reference specified in the regulatory text is incorrect. This document corrects that error. In all other respects, the original document remains the same.

documents.title: Unemployment Insurance Program National Minimum Weekly Work Search Requirements
documents.abstract: The U.S. Department of Labor (Department), through the Employment and Training Administration (ETA), is proposing to amend 20 CFR part 604 both to reflect a 2012 update in Federal law in which Congress, by amending section 303(a) of the Social Security Act (SSA), established a Federal work search requirement; and to establish a national minimum weekly work search requirement standard for the Federal-State unemployment compensation (UC) program. This proposed rule would mandate, among other things, that States require individuals claiming UC to complete at least five qualifying work search activities or, where applicable, meet State-adopted points-based system requirements amounting to five qualifying activities or satisfy equivalent labor force attachment criteria, each week for which UC is claimed; that individuals report their work search activities as part of their certification process prior to payment being issued; and that State law allow for certain qualifying work search activities beyond simply employer contacts. This action is necessary to reduce inconsistencies beyond those created by local labor markets in State- level requirements for individuals to actively seek work. The intended effect is to hold States accountable for administering a UC program that provides temporary wage replacement to eligible individuals while they are actively seeking work through a meaningful engagement with the labor market.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; Bombardier, Inc., Airplanes
documents.abstract: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Bombardier, Inc., Model CL-600-2B16 (604 Variants) airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by reports of cracks being found on the lower wing plank at the rear spar wing station (WS) 59 to WS 65 web and/or flange. This proposed AD would require inspecting the lower wing plank rear spar web and lower flange, the forward surface of the pressure bulkhead frame under the stiffeners, and the vertical stabilizer front spar to frame attachment fitting lower legs for cracks, and repair or rectification if applicable. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus SAS Airplanes
documents.abstract: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Airbus SAS Model A350-941 airplanes. This AD was prompted by a report of a missing main landing gear (MLG) brake rod center pin nut sub-assembly detected during an inspection. This AD requires, depending on airplane configuration, inspection of the MLG brake rod center pin nut, lock ring, and end plate, inspection of the MLG brake rod center pin and nut, and applicable corrective actions. This AD also requires additional work for certain airplanes. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Rules and Regulations, Series 8
Modification of Significant New Uses of Certain Chemical Substances (23-1.M)
documents.abstract: EPA is amending significant new use rules (SNURs) issued under section 5(a)(2) of the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) for certain chemical substances identified herein, which were the subject of premanufacture notices (PMNs) and significant new use notices (SNUNs). This action amends the SNURs by allowing certain new uses reported in the SNUNs or PMNs without additional notification requirements, modifying the significant new use notification requirements based on the actions and determinations for the SNUN or PMN submissions or based on the examination of new test data or other information, and making technical amendments to several SNURs. EPA is issuing these amendments based on review of new and existing data for the chemical substances.

documents.title: Air Plan Approval; Michigan; Determination of Attainment by the Attainment Date for the 2015 Ozone Standards
documents.abstract: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is determining under the Clean Air Act (CAA) that the Detroit, Michigan Moderate nonattainment area ("Detroit area" or "area") attained the 2015 ozone National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS) by the applicable attainment date. This determination relies on the EPA's concurrence on an exceptional events request submitted by the Michigan Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy (EGLE) on February 19, 2026, and concurred on by the EPA on March 24, 2026. Therefore, the EPA is taking final agency action on Michigan's exceptional events request. This action fulfills the EPA's statutory obligation to determine whether the Detroit area attained the 2015 ozone NAAQS by the Moderate attainment date of August 3, 2024.

documents.title: Color Additive Petition From the International Association of Color Manufacturers; Request To Amend the Color Additive Regulations To Remove the Solvents Methylene Chloride, Trichloroethylene, and Ethylene Dichloride
documents.abstract: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or we) is partially granting a color additive petition submitted by the International Association of Color Manufacturers (IACM or petitioner), by amending our color additive regulations, on the basis of abandonment, to remove the authorized uses of methylene chloride, trichloroethylene, and ethylene dichloride from the list of authorized extraction solvents for annatto extract, paprika oleoresin, and turmeric oleoresin. The petitioner provided data demonstrating that these uses have been permanently abandoned. FDA is denying as moot the portion of the petition proposing that the color additive regulations be amended, on the basis of abandonment, to no longer authorize the use of methylene chloride as a diluent in color additive mixtures in inks for marking fruit and vegetables. This request is moot because the authorization for this use has been removed, on the basis of the Delaney Clause, in response to a separate petition.

agencies.name: Health and Human Services Department

documents.title: Color Additive Petition From Environmental Defense Fund et al.; Request To Amend the Color Additive Regulations To Remove the Solvents Ethylene Dichloride, Methylene Chloride, and Trichloroethylene
documents.abstract: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or we) is partially granting a color additive petition submitted by Environmental Defense Fund et al. (petitioners), by amending our color additive regulations, on the basis of the Delaney Clause, to remove the authorized use of methylene chloride as a diluent in color additive mixtures in inks for marking fruit and vegetables. The petitioners provided data demonstrating that this additive induces cancer in laboratory animals. We are denying the remaining petition requests to remove ethylene dichloride, methylene chloride, and trichloroethylene from the list of authorized extraction solvents for annatto extract, paprika oleoresin, and turmeric oleoresin, because any residue of the solvent would be an impurity in the color additive and such impurities are not subject to the Delaney Clause.

documents.title: DCM Impartial Access Requirements
documents.abstract: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission ("Commission" or "CFTC") is issuing an interpretation of the requirement that designated contract markets ("DCMs") provide competitive, open, fair, and impartial access to their members and persons with trading privileges under Commission Regulation 38.151(b) ("Impartial Access Requirements"). Specifically, this final interpretive guidance is being issued to inform the public of the Commission's views on the Impartial Access Requirements that should be guiding exchanges' selections of access criteria. The Commission issues this interpretive guidance after a significant amount of time and effort overseeing the listing and trading of event contracts and other financial assets, as well as monitoring DCM access requirements.

documents.title: Revision of Regulations for Planning, Programming, Budgeting
documents.abstract: The BLM proposes to amend existing regulations that establish the procedures to prepare, revise, or amend land use plans pursuant to the Federal Land Policy and Management Act, as amended (FLPMA). We solicit comment on all aspects of this proposed rule.

documents.title: Information Reporting Regarding Qualified Opportunity Zones and Updated Qualified Opportunity Fund Certification and Decertification Procedures; Correction
documents.abstract: This document contains corrections to the proposed regulations (REG-116506-25), published in the Federal Register on September 11, 2026. These proposed regulations would implement new statutory requirements for qualified opportunity funds to file information returns with the IRS and furnish statements to investors who dispose of investments in those entities and for qualified opportunity zone businesses to furnish statements to qualified opportunity funds that hold interests in them.

documents.title: Medicare and Medicaid Programs; Cutting Administrative Requirements for Excellence in Patient Care
documents.abstract: This proposed rule would reform Medicare and Medicaid regulations deemed obsolete or excessively burdensome on healthcare providers and suppliers, with the objective of reducing costs, enhancing flexibility in delivering innovative care, and streamlining existing regulations. This reform seeks to enable healthcare professionals to devote more resources to improving patient care by eliminating or minimizing requirements that impede quality patient care or that divert resources away from furnishing high quality patient care.

documents.title: Television Broadcasting Services Odessa, Texas
documents.abstract: This document proposes to amend the Table of TV Allotments (Table) of the Federal Communications Commission's (Commission) rules in response to a petition for rulemaking filed by Gray Television Licensee, LLC (Gray), the licensee of KOSA-TV (KOSA-TV), Odessa, Texas (Odessa). Gray held a construction permit to construct a facility on UHF channel 31 at Odessa, and now requests that the Bureau substitute VHF channel 7 for UHF channel 31 in the Table, with the technical parameters as set forth in KOSA-TV's current license. The Media Bureau previously granted a petition for rulemaking submitted by Gray to substitute UHF channel 31 for VHF channel 7 at Odessa. Gray states that it is unable to complete construction of its new channel within the time specified on the construction permit, and therefore requests amendment of the Table to allow it to continue to operate on VHF channel 7 at its currently licensed technical parameters to provide uninterrupted service to viewers. Given that the Licensee proposes to utilize its currently licensed parameters, we believe VHF channel 7 can be substituted for UHF channel 31 at Odessa as proposed, in compliance with the principal community coverage requirements of the Commission's rules. In addition, we find that this channel change meets the technical requirements set forth in the Commission's rules.

documents.title: Security Zones; Protection of Military Cargo, Captain of the Port Zone Puget Sound, WA
documents.abstract: The Coast Guard will enforce security zones for the Protection of Military Cargo from November 8 through November 12, 2026, to provide for the security of life and vessels on navigable waterways during this event. Our regulation for Protection of Military Cargo within the Captain of the Port Zone Puget Sound, WA identifies the security zones for this event in the Blair Waterway and Sitcum Waterway in Commencement Bay, WA. During the enforcement periods, the operator of any vessel in the regulated area must comply with directions from the Captain of the Port or a designated representative.

documents.title: Amendment of Class D and Establishment of Class E Airspace; Chandler and Phoenix, AZ
documents.abstract: This action corrects a final rule published by the FAA in the Federal Register on October 30, 2026, amending the Class D airspace and establishing Class E airspace at Chandler and Phoenix, AZ. Specifically, this action corrects a statement in the preamble of the rule for greater clarity.

documents.title: Pecans Grown in the States of Alabama, Arkansas, Arizona, California, Florida, Georgia, Kansas, Louisiana, Missouri, Mississippi, North Carolina, New Mexico, Oklahoma, South Carolina, and Texas; Changes to Membership and Handling Requirements
documents.abstract: This proposed rule would implement recommendations from the American Pecan Council (Council) to eliminate regional and size designations for sheller members, modify the nomination process for sheller members, adjust the requirements of the inter-handler transfer report form, and establish a late fee and interest charges for unpaid assessments. The rule will also propose two technical corrections.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes
documents.abstract: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain The Boeing Company Model 787-8, 787-9, and 787-10 airplanes. This AD was prompted by reports that the low range radio altimeter (LRRA) system has an increased rate of non-computed data (NCD) outputs at low altitudes during approach and landing, which could cause unreliable altimeter function. This AD requires replacing the left and right LRRA transmit and receive coaxial cables with larger gauge coaxial cables. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Pacific Island Fisheries; Commercial Fishing in the Pacific Remote Islands Marine National Monument Expansion
documents.abstract: NMFS proposes to amend regulations that prohibit commercial fishing in the Pacific Remote Islands Marine National Monument Expansion (PRIMNM Expansion), which comprises waters of the U.S. exclusive economic zone (EEZ) between 50 to 200 nautical miles (nmi; 93 to 370 kilometers (km)) around Johnston Atoll and Wake and Jarvis Islands. This action is necessary to conform fishing regulations with Presidential Proclamation 10918 of April 17, 2025--Unleashing American Commercial Fishing in the Pacific, as amended by Presidential Proclamation 11035 of June 11, 2026--Restoring American Commercial Fishing in the Pacific, and in light of a court order. Fisheries in the PRIMNM Expansion would be regulated pursuant to existing fishing regulations under the Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act (Magnuson-Stevens Act), the Western and Central Pacific Fisheries Convention Implementation Act (WCPFCIA), the South Pacific Tuna Act (SPTA), and other applicable laws, that apply to all U.S. commercial fishing vessels but were superseded and made inapplicable when the commercial fishing prohibition for the PRIMNM Expansion was established. The proposed rule supports the long-term sustainability of U.S. fisheries and provides for the proper care and management of the PRIMNM and PRIMNM Expansion and the objects of historic or scientific interest therein, as directed by Proclamation 10918, as amended by Proclamation 11035.

documents.title: Threshold for the Requirement To Collect, Retain, and Transmit Information on Funds Transfers and Transmittals of Funds That Begin or End Outside the United States, and Clarification of the Requirement To Collect, Retain, and Transmit Information on Transactions Involving Convertible Virtual Currencies and Digital Assets With Legal Tender Status; Withdrawal
documents.abstract: FinCEN and the Board (collectively, the "Agencies") are withdrawing the joint notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM) published on October 27, 2020, that proposed modifying the threshold in the Agencies' rules implementing the Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) requiring financial institutions to collect and retain information on certain funds transfers and transmittals of funds. The NPRM would have reduced this threshold from $3,000 to $250 for funds transfers and transmittals of funds that begin or end outside the United States. FinCEN additionally proposed reducing from $3,000 to $250 the threshold in FinCEN's rule requiring financial institutions to transmit to other financial institutions in the payment chain information on funds transfers and transmittals of funds that begin or end outside the United States. The NPRM also would have clarified the meaning of "money" as used in the Agencies' rules to specify that the rules apply to domestic and cross-border transactions involving convertible virtual currency (CVC) and digital assets that have legal tender status to a recipient. The Agencies will not take further action on this NPRM.

documents.title: Medicare Program; Implementation of Sections 6219, 6220, and 6224 of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026; Correction
documents.abstract: This document corrects a typographical error in the proposed rule that appeared in the October 20, 2026 Federal Register titled "Medicare Program; Implementation of Sections 6219, 6220, and 6224 of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026".

documents.title: Extension of the Suspension of Expansion of End-User Controls for Affiliates of Certain Listed Entities
documents.abstract: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is extending the suspension of the interim final rule (IFR), "Expansion of End-User Controls to Cover Affiliates of Certain Listed Entities." The suspension was set to end November 9, 2026. This final rule extends the suspension through January 10, 2027.

documents.title: Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program and Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Program
documents.abstract: This rule finalizes and codifies the Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program ("Negotiation Program") and establishes certain new policies for the Negotiation Program and the Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Program ("Part D Program") as required by the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022. This final rule also finalizes a proposed policy for specific fixed combination drugs that are new formulations.
